key_insight: Feasibility verifiers do not generalize equally across reaction sources: performance depends strongly on where the candidate reaction came from, and no single model wins everywhere.
engineering_relevance: For automated reaction planning pipelines, verifier choice and training data must be matched to the proposal source, or good candidates may be incorrectly rejected while infeasible ones slip through.
method: Built FREA, a benchmark of 751 expert-labeled reactions spanning retrosynthesis proposals, zero-yield records, LLM edits, and five negative-generation methods.
Compared forward models and LLM-based verifiers under an explicit chemist-defined feasibility criterion.
Released a larger training corpus of 14M+ recorded reactions plus generated negatives to study negative supervision effects.
evidence_signal: Across source-specific evaluations, LLMs with only the criterion were competitive, forward models did best on retrosynthesis proposals, and both forward models fell below chance on separating infeasible alternative disconnections from feasible generated candidates.
watch_item: Improvements from adding generated negatives were source-dependent, so gains on synthetic candidates did not reliably transfer to retrosynthesis proposal screening.
paper_title: FREA: A Multi-Source Expert Benchmark for Reaction Feasibility Verification
